title: Bare, non-union logical types through reconstruct(): date and timestamp-millis still encode
rationale: Carries the shape that avro-logical-type-datum-is-writable-control used to have and gave up when it was repointed at its control's own byte-identical schema. Every other logical type in the corpus's DATUM coverage is wrapped in a two-branch nullable union, and union resolution is a different code path from a bare type: resolveUnionBranch picks a branch before convertLogicalType ever runs. Deleting the bare shape to fix a wording defect would have been a silent coverage loss, so it is a row rather than a footnote.
catchesBugClass: A logical-type conversion that only works because a union wrapper normalised the value first, and a writer rejection that only appears on the bare branch. Paired with the union-wrapped control it separates 'logical types work' from 'nullable unions work'.
cannotCatch: Two logical types only - date and timestamp-millis. It says nothing about time-millis, time-micros, timestamp-micros, uuid or decimal, all of which the union-wrapped control covers, and nothing about a logical type inside an array or a map.

predicted.detail: No nested record and no union to resolve, so the one-level copy is sufficient; the datum should validate and encode exactly as it did before the twin was repointed.
